attributes.text: In angelic lore the Angel Ramiel has been described as the Angel of True Vision.

As an Archangel, Ramiel is known to assist us with the interpretation and comprehension of various communications in such a way as to find a positive perception within. Connected with historians, scholars, and archaeologists she is known for preserving and illustrating our history

Celebrated as the Goddess of truth and justice, Ma’at is recognized for her ability to create balance and equilibrium in all that she touches. It is said that she prevented the universe from reverting to chaos and is known to the Gods as the mediator. Due to her abilities as an adjudicator, she was tasked with assessing the deeds of the dead.

She is known to be diplomatic and graceful in social affairs and adapt in dealing with authorities, she is sympathetic and emboldened with sincerity and gratitude.

Throughout many belief systems, the stories of angels make up a part of our heritage, existing as important mystical beings sharing spiritual messages.
In the angelic realm, the Archangel Sariel originates principally from Judaic tradition, her Hebrew name translates as “God’s Command” and appears in the Talmud as well as other sacred Jewish texts.
The Dead Sea Scrolls, lists her name among others as written upon the shields of soldiers invoked for her protective powers in Jewish and early Christian texts.
Considered one of the archangels who rule Earth, she is linked with the skies and the celestial forms, holding sacred knowledge concerning the Moon.

While considered a holy angel with primordial powers, she is known to be one of the nine angels of the summer equinox and rules the zodiacal sign of the Ram; Aries. In The Book of Enoch, the ancient Hebrew apocalyptic text sighting material on the origins of demons and giants, Sariel is said to be one of the holy angels who watch over other spirits, and who “look upon the bloodshed on Earth”. She is considered to be a holy Archangel also known as the “Angel of Punishment and Death” and believed to be tasked with punishing both mortals and angels who violate God’s commands.
A warrior angel she is both holy and fallen, believed to be a kind angel of death and an angel of healing, bring both hope and comfort, retribution and protection.

Leylah was among the very first pieces created in the Spirit collection. At the beginning of this series these works had no interior elements, and even the concepts behind the artworks were only developing. The idea that the interior landscape was to take importance in the work allowed the inside of the bronze to become a focal point, and as the notion of the spirit was developing is evident in this work by the absence of any inner structure.

As one of the very first works in this collection, I thought it fitting to name her after the Angel of Conception, who is believed to watch over the new born spirit from conception to birth and oversees and protects childbirth.
The Angel of fertility, love, war, and sex

Considered as one of the more powerful sky deities, she was the divine personification of the planet Venus. A heavenly being, to both the Assyrians and Babylonians, Ishtar was the goddess of fertility, love, war, and sex. During the reign of Constantine and the Christianisation of the lands Easter was created from the mythology surrounding the goddess Ishtar.
Bronze by Blake Ward and Boky Hackel
One Quarter Life-size Partial Female Figure

The Cat Goddess and solar deity linked with fertility, childbirth and perfume. Widely adored in Egypt, she was thought to be able to shield women and property from misfortune and was seen as the custodian of love. In Egyptian Heterography Bastet is depicted as a cat or a woman with a cat's head and was believed to be the protector of Lower Egypt.
Bronze by Blake Ward and Boky Hackel
The Angel Hael inspires art, and beauty. Although never mentioned in the scriptures, she is considered a modern addition to traditional angelic lore and is thought to inspire the kindness in mankind.
Bronze Blake Ward and Boky Hackel

This work is dedicated to the life of Fatimah Baraghani (1814 -1852), an influential poet and theologian of the Baha Faith in Iran. Her life, influence and execution made her a key figure of the religion. Described as "the first woman suffrage martyr” and as an example of courage in the struggle for women's rights.

Spirits Collection carries the figure forward by exposing the interior of the sculpture and thus addressing that which lies within us, creating partial figures by retaining only a fragment of the whole. Seeing our interior features as one of the most vital parts of our existence he addresses humanity and our human condition, while remaining true to his foundation and the tenets of classical figurative sculpture.
Bronze by Blake Ward and Boky Hackel

An early Egyptian deity, Neith was considered the creator of the universe and mother of all Gods. She was said to have both female traits, as well as the masculine energy required in creation. Associated with wisdom, the cosmos, water, hunting, war, and fate as well as many of the domestic arts. One myth insinuates that she created the world by weaving it. The Warrior characteristic within Neith was considered an arbitrator and protector of the people, she also cared for the dead and helped to prepare their souls for the afterlife.
Bronze by Blake Ward and Boky Hackel

A Goddess of Healing and occasionally referred to as the Lady of the Sea. Considered a sacred feminine in several ancient religious beliefs, Asherah is thought of as a mother figure as well as a goddess in some Egyptian, Hittite, Philistine and Arabic texts.
By Blake Ward and Boky Hackel
One of three princesses of the Third Heaven

Dalquielle was trained in fine graces as a means of protecting her public dignity. Using her beauty to advantage, she is outwardly flirtatious and covets attention, still she often remains apart and alone so as to conceal her dark side. This inexplicable element of her personality is shrouded in secrecy and mystery. She is known to be a courageous yet fierce opponent.
Bronze by Blake Ward and Boky Hackel

The Angel of Eloquence helps us to distinguish the possible from the impossible and assists us by indicating which of our aspirations will be appropriate, constructive and genuine.
Angelic lore credits him with the rejuvenation of our inspirations and he is known to support and protect the undecided among us from the temptation to live by illicit means.
He encourages reflection and detachment from events so as to perceive the reality and has the capacity to materialize thoughts through our deeds.
Known for his grace, eloquence and conviction, he grants forgiveness and solace for our sins.
Bronze by Blake Ward and Boky Hackel

The Archangel Azrael is known in Angelic lore to assist us in our passage from the material to the spiritual world. Often an arduous transition, Azrael brings comfort and guidance to those seeking their way. Azrael offers those who seek his guidance, comfort, and inspiration. He serves as a bridge to the spiritual realm offering thoughts and experiences that provide us with guidance. To find him one needs only to look inside yourself.
Bronze by Blake Ward & Boky Hackel
